note: Run each test prompt with the skill installed and without it, then compare against the expectations. should_trigger and should_not_trigger check the description routing.

should_trigger: set up this repo for agents
I just cloned this project, map the codebase for me
create an AGENTS.md for this Flutter app

tests.prompt: Onboard me to this Next.js repo and set up AGENTS.md.
expectations: Detects Next.js and package manager from files, not by asking
Prints a short mirror of findings before asking anything
Marks each command verified or unverified
Writes CLAUDE.md containing only @AGENTS.md
Shows the draft before writing
Saves a note under .agent-notes/repo-scout/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'
Creates the folder only on first write and writes no secrets

should_trigger: debug this: LateInitializationError on the home screen
works locally but 500s in production
why is this list janky

tests.prompt: My Laravel queue job sometimes sends the email twice. Debug it.
expectations: Builds or proposes a deterministic red-capable loop before theorising
Lists 3 to 5 ranked hypotheses that each make a prediction
States the root cause with evidence before editing
Uses a tagged [BH-xxxx] for temporary logs and removes them
Redacts any secrets shown
Saves a note under .agent-notes/bug-hunter/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'
Creates the folder only on first write and writes no secrets

should_trigger: brainstorm features for a habit tracker
should I use Riverpod or BLoC
grill me on this plan

tests.prompt: I'm thinking of adding offline sync to my Flutter app. Poke holes in it.
expectations: Chooses Grill mode and says so
Asks one question at a time with a recommended answer
Looks up facts in the repo instead of asking
Ends with a settled-decisions list and waits for confirmation
Saves a note under .agent-notes/branch-storm/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'
Creates the folder only on first write and writes no secrets

should_trigger: review this design
is this button color okay?
make this screen look more professional

tests.prompt: Is the grey text on this white card readable?
expectations: Uses Quick mode: verdict, principle, exact fix value

Mentions at most 2 other P1 issues

should_trigger: audit my Flutter app for performance
why is scrolling janky on Android
review these mobile screens

tests.prompt: My Flutter product list drops frames. Audit it.
expectations: Every finding has a file:line
Asks for or recommends profile-mode measurement on a real device
Lists other usages before proposing a shared-widget change
Stops after the plan and asks for a path
Saves a note under .agent-notes/frame-budget/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'
Creates the folder only on first write and writes no secrets

should_trigger: open a PR for this
commit and push my changes
write the PR description

tests.prompt: Commit this and open a merge request. Tracker is Linear, ticket ENG-42.
expectations: Detects the host from the remote
Runs a self-review of the diff and the profile's checks
Uses conventional commit messages
Includes Closes ENG-42 in the body
Shows host, base, title and body and waits before creating the MR
Saves a note under .agent-notes/shipwright/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'
Creates the folder only on first write and writes no secrets

tests.prompt: Use shipwright: create branch feat/ENG-42-cart-rounding, commit my changes with conventional commits, push, and open a PR into main. Ticket ENG-42 (Linear). Open it as a draft.
expectations: Creates the branch with the exact name given
Uses main as the base
Opens the PR as a draft
Includes Closes ENG-42 or Refs ENG-42 in the body
Prints the plan (host, head, base, title, body) before the first external action
Writes the PR body to .agent-notes/shipwright/ and passes it with --body-file or the API

should_trigger: improve this prompt: make the app faster
write a prompt for an agent to add dark mode
enhance my prompt

tests.prompt: Make my prompt better: add search to the products page
expectations: Gathers context from the repo and AGENTS.md instead of asking
Output has a one-sentence goal and checkable acceptance criteria
Assumptions are listed separately from the prompt
Does not execute the prompt
Compiled prompt is not padded
Saves a note under .agent-notes/prompt-compiler/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'
Creates the folder only on first write and writes no secrets

should_trigger: what should I run next
which skill do I use for this
where am I in the workflow

tests.prompt: I just finished brainstorming the checkout redesign. What now?
expectations: Reads AGENTS.md and the newest notes before answering
Quotes the evidence (a note path or profile fact)
Recommends exactly one next skill (task-graph) and at most two side entries
Reads the recommended skill's SKILL.md first
Reply is 8 lines or fewer

should_trigger: write a spec for this feature
break this down into tasks
create tickets for the offline sync work

tests.prompt: We decided on offline-first sync. Turn it into a spec and tasks. Tracker is Linear, key ENG.
expectations: Reads the latest branch-storm note
Task 1 is a thin end-to-end slice, not a layer
Every task has pass or fail acceptance criteria and a Blocked by line
Lists the frontier and checks for cycles
Shows the spec and tasks and waits before writing or creating tickets
Saves a note under .agent-notes/task-graph/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'

should_trigger: implement the login form
add this feature test-first
write tests for the cart service

tests.prompt: Implement task 01: user can add an item to the cart.
expectations: Restates acceptance criteria as observable behaviors
Writes one failing test first and shows it failing for the expected reason
Writes minimal code, then runs the test
Does not write all tests up front
Mocks only at system boundaries
Runs lint, types and the full suite and reports real results
Saves a note under .agent-notes/tdd-loop/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'

should_trigger: review my changes before I open a PR
is this ready to merge
check my diff

tests.prompt: Review my branch before I ship it.
expectations: Runs the profile's checks and reports real results
Maps each acceptance criterion to code and a test
Every finding has a file:line and evidence and was verified by reading the code
Separates problems the diff introduced from pre-existing ones
Ends with a verdict: ready, ready with notes or fix first
Does not edit code unless asked
Saves a note under .agent-notes/diff-review/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'

should_trigger: are we ready to release
pre-release checklist
cut a release

tests.prompt: Run the release checklist for the Flutter app.
expectations: Suggests a semver bump from the commit types since the last tag
Drafts a changelog from commit subjects
Marks each checklist item pass, fail or unknown with evidence, never assumed
Lists one-way doors and a rollback plan
States GO, GO with risks or NO-GO
Does not tag, publish or deploy
Saves a note under .agent-notes/release-gate/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'

should_trigger: hand this off to another agent
save my progress, I'll continue tomorrow
write a handoff note

tests.prompt: Hand this off. Next session will finish the tests.
expectations: Links other notes instead of duplicating them
Records decisions with reasons and what was tried and failed
Every command and path in the note was verified
Redacts secrets
Ends with a one-line starter prompt
Saves a note under .agent-notes/agent-handoff/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'

should_trigger: what did my partner do since my last commit
did anyone push
catch me up on the repo

tests.prompt: What did my teammates push since my last commit?
expectations: Uses the date of the user's last commit as the anchor and says so
Runs git fetch only and never pulls, merges or rebases
States that only pushed commits are visible, not local or uncommitted work
Groups pushed commits per person and branch with a short summary
Reports overlap with the user's changed files and the merge-tree conflict probe result
Uses names, not email addresses, in the saved note
Saves a note under .agent-notes/peer-sync/ using the template in references/output-format.md and ends with 'Saved: <path>'
